title: Local structure of the chosen strict-henselization colimit
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. The chosen coordinate-ring colimit $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] admits a local-ring structure and is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. No identification of its residue field or factorization of the geometric point is asserted here.

source.place: Tag 04HX, with algebra.tex Tags 04GW and 04GP; online text read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04HX and /tag/04GW and /tag/04GP

proof.text: Choose an affine open Spec A containing the image of the geometric point. Its entire image lies there because Spec Omega has a single point, so factor the point through that open. Put p equal to the resulting prime and K equal to the relative separable closure of its residue field in Omega.

source.place: Tag 04HX, with algebra.tex Tags 04GW and 04GP; online text read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04HX and /tag/04GW and /tag/04GP

proof.text: Apply etale_local_ring_triples to obtain colimit cocones cn and ct on affine neighbourhoods and residue triples, and the isomorphism s:cn.pt -> ct.pt. Apply strictHenselization_triples to get another colimit cocone c on the identical triple diagram, together with its local and strictly henselian structures.

source.place: Tag 04HX, with algebra.tex Tags 04GW and 04GP; online text read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04HX and /tag/04GW and /tag/04GP

proof.text: The small representative functor followed by strictHenselizationAffineInclusion is an equivalence. Its opposite pulls the all-affine coordinate diagram back definitionally to strictHenselizationDiagram. HasColimit.isoOfEquivalence and colimit.isoColimitCocone identify the chosen strictHenselizationRing with cn.pt. Compose with s and the unique comparison of ct with c. Transfer local and strictly henselian structures along the inverse ring equivalence, then transport along the equation saying the chosen affine factorization is barY.
